notes: SAE International is a US standards body for aerospace and automotive engineering, publishing Aerospace Recommended Practices (ARP), Aerospace Standards (AS) and Aerospace Information Reports (AIR). Note that ISO/SAE 21434 (road vehicle cybersecurity engineering) is jointly published and is registered under the ISO namespace at secid:control/iso.org/21434. Documents are paywalled.

match_nodes.description: ARP4754A — Guidelines for Development of Civil Aircraft and Systems

data.notes: System-level development assurance for civil aircraft. Defines Development Assurance Level (DAL) and its Function (FDAL) and Item (IDAL) variants, and permits allocating a lower IDAL to individual items where architecture provides sufficient independence. Revision B was published in 2023. Paired with EUROCAE ED-79A.

children.description: DAL — Development Assurance Level. The assurance-rigour classification used across the ARP4754A / ARP4761 / DO-178C set.

data.notes: Five levels, A (most rigorous, catastrophic failure condition) through E (no safety effect), assigned from the failure-condition severity established by the ARP4761 safety assessment. Terminology varies by document and this is a common source of confusion: ARP4754A defines Development Assurance Level and its Function (FDAL) and Item (IDAL) variants; DO-178C itself says "software level"; DO-254 says "hardware design assurance level". Unlike CVSS, DAL carries no environmental adjustment — it is not lowered by adding a perimeter control, only by architectural change that alters the failure-condition classification, which ARP4754A permits via IDAL allocation across sufficiently independent items.

match_nodes.description: ARP4761 — Guidelines and Methods for Conducting the Safety Assessment Process on Civil Airborne Systems and Equipment

data.notes: The safety assessment methods that feed ARP4754A and DO-178C: Functional Hazard Assessment (FHA), Preliminary System Safety Assessment (PSSA), System Safety Assessment (SSA), plus fault tree analysis, FMEA and common cause analysis. Establishes the five-tier failure-condition severity classification (Catastrophic, Hazardous/Severe-Major, Major, Minor, No Safety Effect) from which DAL is derived. Revision A was published in 2023.
